summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/214)

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Ḥalyo! Akit w kmətyaqnono ste laqət ġalabe qetre bu fəlḥono d hani ḥṣar (10) əšne, kəpli d əmmono d kofəlḥat Ǧan.
data.translation: Atiya Xamri: Fine! Certainly, and I am convinced too, you have met very many difficulties in the work of these ten (10) years, I can say, that you have been working, Jan.

rationale: New I.2 general work in a ten-year communal/cultural context; first I Infectum box. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/235)

data.turoyo: Kəbʕono d faytono la kmo šəwole d kətli ste l ḥabro Isḥoq Baroše. Xəd mərlan bi badaye, xəd mawḏaʕlox ruḥox, hat ste hani zabno yarixo kofəlḥat bayn du ʕamayḏan.
data.translation: I want to enter into a few questions I also have for our friend Isḥoq Baroše. As we said at the beginning, as you introduced yourself, you too have been working among our people for this long time.

rationale: Independent support for new I.2: long-term work among the community, no agricultural object. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 2: arbeiten, tätig sein (auch in der kulturellen Arbeit für die Gemeinschaft)

data.gloss: arbeiten, tätig sein (auch in der kulturellen Arbeit für die Gemeinschaft)

rationale: Two direct addresses describe ten years/long-term activity by Jan and Isḥoq among the community, with no cultivated field or agricultural activity. This provides the contrast missing in round 1.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Ishaq Material culture/5)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr məd aṯino šġili bu+bayto, fləḥli, šġili bu+bayto ʕam emi, ʕam babi, hēš baḥ+ḥàyene. Karme, šuġlo, mə‿dhowewa.
data.translation: After I came back, I worked at home, I farmed, I worked at home with my mother, with my father, they are still alive. Vineyards, work, whatever there was.

rationale: Thin Preterit/1 cell; first-person agricultural work with the cultivated object omitted and vineyards specified nearby.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Kmaḥwe, bi Addane m zawno yo, m zawno azze. Bi Addane əlla mu floḥo w mu hno w mak kətone w mu zroʕo mede lə saymiwo bi Addane. Ṣənayəʕ i naqqayo latwo. Balki bəṯər, uʕdo hawi bi Addane, hayo ġer.
data.translation: Khori Brahim: Apparently he had been in Adana a long time, he went long ago. In Adana, apart from farming and so on, cotton and sowing, they used to do nothing. There were no industries at that time. Perhaps afterwards, now things have developed in Adana; that is different.

rationale: Infinitiv 1 has only one grammar example after round 1; Adana agriculture is opposed to industries, retaining the agricultural meaning. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: The L-series -li marks the first-person actor. The edition’s farmed is broader than a single ploughing operation, but one objectless autobiographical token does not establish a separate lexical sense.

The new general-work sense is justified by nonagricultural addressees and community-domain phrases, not by the English work alone. It resolves the round-1 question about a possible wider meaning with contrastive new evidence.
Unreduced ko-fəlḥat and the neighboring fəlḥono noun fit the interview on cultural activity. No additional stem or Nomen Actionis box is inferred merely from that neighboring noun.
The collective u ʕamayḏan as actor in 4.II/908 extends I.2; subsequent self-repair around maḥwe does not license a separate achieve/progress sense for flḥ.

Does objectless fləḥli conventionally mean agricultural work more broadly than ploughing, or does the vineyard context supply the omitted cultivation object? More contrastive evidence is needed before widening the numbered gloss.

Do speakers distinguish the general-work use as a learned/literary usage from ordinary agricultural flḥ, or is it common in speech as well? Confirm the range beyond the community-work contexts supplied here.
Absolute agricultural use with no expressed field object; the following vineyards context supports cultivation rather than a new general-work meaning.
Infinitiv floḥo in the Adana list remains agricultural, beside cotton and sowing and opposed to industries. It supports broader farming within sense 1 without changing its inherited gloss.
